MRI of left knee with -Locator, SG PD FatSat, SG T2W FS, SG T1W, CO T2W FS, AX T2W FS

Findings:
> The contour of anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments appearing within normal limit
> High signal intensity in medial and lateral meniscus without significant extending to the surface, probably due to myxoid degeneration
> Bony fragement in posterior knee joint, suspecious of loose body.
> Spur formation in left knee joint and patella with subchondral edema and cysts, indicating osteoarthritis.
> Full thickness cartilage loss of patella, suggestive of chondromalacia
> Large amount of joint effusion with suprapatellar bursitis 

Impression:
1. Osteoarthritis of left knee joint
2. Suspect intra-articular loose body in posterior knee joint
3. Myxoid degeneration of medial and lateral meniscus
4. Chondromalacia of patella cartilage
5. Large amount of joint effusion with suprapatellar bursitis 

Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation and further evaluation.

Antecedentes Clínicos:
Meniscopatía interna.
Hallazgos:
Ligamentos cruzados y colaterales dentro de límites conservados.
Amputación marginal del cuerno posterior y parte del cuerpo del menisco lateral asociado a
imagen de rotura horizontal del cuerno posterior del menisco lateral.
Rotura compleja degenerativa de predominio marginal del cuerpo y cuerno posterior del menisco
medial con moderada extrusión meniscal. Esto se asocia a edema de las partes blandas
regionales.
Úlceras condrales de espesor parcial y total de la zona de carga del compartimento femorotibial
medial con cambios óseos secundarios predominando la zona de carga del cóndilo femoral medial
y periférico del platillo tibial medial.
Cartílagos del compartimento femorotibial lateral y patelofemoral sin alteraciones significativas.
Leve derrame articular. No hay quistes poplíteos patológicos.
Tendones cuadricipital, rotuliano, tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial
dentro de límites normales.
No hay alteración de señal de la grasa de Hoffa.
Impresión:
Amputación marginal del menisco lateral con rotura horizontal del cuerno posterior del menisco
lateral, no desplazada.
Rotura compleja degenerativa del menisco medial con moderada extrusión meniscal.
Condropatía lesiones grado 3 y 4 del compartimento femorotibial medial.
Leve derrame articular

Right knee MRI:

INDICATION: Assess block knee and context of known medial meniscus injury.

COMPARISON: Compare with right knee radiographs from [Date].

FINDINGS:

Moderate right knee effusion. No Baker's cyst.

ANTERIOR COMPARTMENT:
Preserved cartilage. Extensor mechanism is intact. Minimal soft tissue infiltration surrounding the anterior aspect of the knee. Prominent medial plica without definite insinuation into the patellofemoral compartment.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Preserved cartilage. Bucket-handle tear involving the anterior horn, body and posterior horn of medial meniscus with a flipped fragment in the intercondylar notch. The flipped fragment measures around 2.1 x 0.5 x 0.6 cm. Medial collateral ligament partially covered on the field of view appears intact. Partially covered pes anserine tendons are also intact.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Preserved cartilage. No discrete meniscal tear. Lateral collateral ligament, popliteus tendons, and biceps femoris tendons are intact. Iliotibial band unremarkable.

INTERCONDYLAR COMPARTMENT:
Anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament are intact.

Portions visualized of muscle bulk and may neurovascular structures are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:
1. Bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus with displaced fragment in the intercondylar notch. No significant chondrosis. No other meniscal fragment visualized.
2. Moderate knee joint effusion
3. Lateral meniscus is intact.

MRI of right Knee with 
-Locator, SG PD FatSat, SG T2W FS, SG T1W, AX T2W FS, CO T2W FS



> Spur formation and subchondral bone marrow edema of knee and irregular thining of intra-articular cartilage and some intra-articular loose bodies, reflecting osteoarthritis of knee, more severe at patellofemoral joint and lateral femorotibial joint .
> The contour of ACL in a straight line and increase signal intensity inside on F/S T2WI, in favor of grade 1 injury or mucoid degeneration.
> The contour of PCL appears to be within normal, no abnormal signal intensity is noted.
> Small size of medial meniscal root with increased signal  on F/S T2WI, R/O tear.
    Linear signal intensity in anterior horn of lateral meniscus, without significant extending into the surface, in favor of  grade 2 intrasubstance signal , maybe due to degeneration.
> Both medial & lateral collateral ligaments appear to be within normal.
> Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis with suprapatellar and medial plicae; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis. Small Baker's cyst
> Increased fat stranding and minimal fluid accumulation located along the pes anserinus, R/O Anserine bursitis

Impression: 
1. Osteoarthritis of right knee, more prominent at lateral compartment with grade 4 chondromalacia.
2. R/O medial meniscal root tear; degeneration of lateral meniscus.
3. Synovitis of right knee and suprapatellar bursitis and patellar plicae.
4. Small Baker's cyst and anserine bursitis.
5. Grade 1 injury or degeneration of ACL.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation

 The lateral compartment, there is radial tear at the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. There is focal high grade chondral injury (more than 50% thickness cartilage loss) at the posterolateral tibial plateau (about 1.7*1.7 cm).  
 The patellofemoral joint appears congruent. There is no cartilage injury. The medial patellofemoral ligament is intact.  
 There is complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament, at mid substance. The posterior cruciate ligament is intact. There is anterior tibial translation. 
 The medial and lateral collateral ligament complexes are intact. The posteromedial oblique ligament is intact. The meniscopopliteal fascicles are intact. The popliteofibular ligament is intact. 
 The extensor mechanism is normal.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Minimal distal quadriceps tendinosis.
2.	No acute osseous, meniscal or ligamentous injury. No significant chondrosis.

CLINICAL HISTORY:Six-week history of instability right knee. Assess for collateral ligament tear.

PROCEDURE:Multisequence multiplanar unenhanced MRI of the right knee according to routine protocol.

IMAGING FINDINGS:

Slight peripheral extrusion of the medial meniscal body without discrete medial meniscal tear. The lateral meniscus is intact.

Intact anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament.

The medial collateral ligament, posterior oblique ligament, fibular collateral ligament, biceps femoris tendon insertion, and iliotibial band are intact. Low-grade partial-thickness tear of the proximal fibers of the fibular collateral ligament.

The patellar retinacula are intact. No femoral trochlear dysplasia. The TT-TG distance measures 11 mm, within normal limits. The quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact.

Tiny focus of full-thickness cartilage denuding at the patellar apex. Scattered foci of mild chondrosis throughout the remainder of the patellar articular surface. Preserved medial and lateral femorotibial articular cartilage. Tiny bone island medial femoral condyle.

Trace knee joint fluid. Regional musculature is within normal limits. No suspicious focal marrow signal alteration.

IMPRESSION:
1. Low-grade partial-thickness tear of the proximal fibers of the lateral collateral ligament.
2. Subtle patellofemoral chondrosis as described.
